description: ¡Somos KillaTech! Un equipo multidisciplinario de Cochabamba apasionado por la tecnología, el desarrollo web y las ciencias de la Tierra. En este NASA Space Apps 2026, estamos desarrollando "TUNARI-SAR", un sistema predictivo de alerta temprana ante desbordes y deslizamientos para el Parque Nacional Tunari y el municipio. Buscamos compañeros proactivos con habilidades en desarrollo frontend/backend, GIS, análisis de datos o diseño para potenciar este MVP de impacto local y global.
summary:
During every rainy season, the mountain streams (torrenteras) and slopes of Tunari National Park in Cochabamba (Taquiña, Pintumayu, Pajcha, Chijllawiri, and Cota 2,750) experience flash floods, debris flows, and landslides. Dense storm clouds blind conventional optical satellites, delaying preventive warnings.

Team KillaTech developed TUNARI-SAR, an interactive geospatial early warning platform that fuses Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR/Sentinel-1), capable of penetrating cloud cover to measure subsurface soil saturation and ground micro-deformation—with topographic slope models (NASA SRTM DEM) and real-time precipitation estimates (NASA GPM IMERG).

The multi-criteria index was calibrated and validated against 60 historical ground-truth points from the Autonomous Municipal Government of Cochabamba (GAMC), achieving 88.3% early detection accuracy. The tool democratizes hazard monitoring for municipal authorities and local community organizations (OTBs) without requiring expensive physical sensors in every ravine.
details:
What does TUNARI-SAR do and how does it work?

TUNARI-SAR is an interactive early warning web platform designed to predict flash floods, debris flows (mazamorras), and landslides across the mountain streams (torrenteras) and slopes of Tunari National Park (Cochabamba, Bolivia), including critical hotspots such as Taquiña, Pintumayu, Pajcha, Chijllawiri, and Cota 2,750.

During intense convective storms, dense cloud cover completely blinds conventional optical satellites. To overcome this barrier, TUNARI-SAR fuses three NASA open data layers through a real-time weighted multi-criteria index:

Synthetic Aperture Radar (NASA NISAR / Sentinel-1): Penetrates cloud cover and heavy rain to detect antecedent subsurface soil moisture and terrain micro-deformation (35% weight).

Digital Elevation Model (NASA SRTM 30m DEM): Evaluates critical slopes, micro-watershed morphometry, and runoff accumulation (35% weight).

Satellite Precipitation (NASA GPM IMERG): Estimates and simulates hourly rainfall intensity in mm/h (30% weight).

Through an interactive satellite simulator, municipal operators and community leaders can model rainfall scenarios (light, storm, or extreme) and instantly visualize the risk level of each watershed under three operational protocols: Stable (<55%), Caution (55%–74%), and Critical (≥75%).

Scientific Validation, Benefits, and Expected Impact

The model was calibrated and validated using a Ground-Truth methodology against 60 georeferenced historical flood and mass-wasting points from the Autonomous Municipal Government of Cochabamba (GAMC), achieving an early detection accuracy of 88.3%.

Benefits: Democratizes geospatial monitoring without requiring the installation or maintenance of expensive physical sensors in inaccessible ravines.

Impact: Directly protects over 20,700 residents across Cochabamba's metropolitan influence zones and provides an open architecture scalable throughout the entire Andes mountain range.

Tools, Programming Languages, and Software Used

Frontend & Geospatial Visualization: Next.js 16 (App Router), React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet with Esri World Imagery satellite mapping.

Processing & Data: NASA open datasets (NISAR/Sentinel-1, SRTM DEM, GPM IMERG) and GAMC's georeferenced historical inventory structured in JSON.

Deployment & Open Source: Cloud hosting on Vercel and a public repository under the MIT License on GitHub: https://github.com/FranzMindef2023/tunari-sar

Creativity and Factors Considered by the Team

The creativity of TUNARI-SAR lies in translating complex SAR interferometry and backscatter data into an intuitive, actionable decision-making dashboard for local authorities (Risk Management Unit - UGR, Civil Defense) and Grassroots Territorial Organizations (OTBs). Our team accounted for critical local realities: the steep topography of the Tunari massif, prior soil saturation ahead of extreme rainfall, limited municipal budgets for physical instrumentation, and the need for a lightweight web platform that loads rapidly even over mobile field connections.
